session_reading: A two-phase day on the AS chip. Morning: a five-run power/frequency-window hunt for q8/q9 — the opening window (#7) had its floor too high to resolve q8's dressed branch; deepening and widening (#8) produced one false success (q8 locked onto a narrow power-independent spur ~22 MHz off) and one chaotic-top failure (q9); the -70-floor wide-span run (#9) drowned both in noise; only the narrow-span pair #10/#11 produced trustworthy answers. The settled recipe (pmin=-45, pmax=-15) then swept q3-q7 cleanly in one run (#12). Evening: q5-q8 were re-calibrated after the chip's bias state moved the resonators a few MHz; #232's -60 floor pinned two optima to the scan's bottom edge and #233 (floor -45) immediately fixed them. Net: the day worked, but roughly half the runs were window-tuning overhead, and q9 was never re-verified against the evening chip state.
taxonomy_gaps: NEW:spur-lock — the analysis latches onto a narrow, power-INDEPENDENT spike (interference spur / normalization artifact, an upward spike in the line cuts, not a dip) far from the real resonator and reports SUCCESS (#8 q8). C5 covers real neighboring resonator lines, not non-resonator artifacts; this is the dangerous false-accept class.

NEW:noise-floor — the power floor extends below the usable readout noise floor, so the bottom rows are pure speckle; the dressed branch is inside the window but its SNR falls below the gate (#9 both qubits, bottom of #10). C2/C3 describe the window missing the physics; this is the window outrunning the signal.

NEW:bottom-edge-optimum — the map is clean C1 yet the reported optimal power sits at/near the scan's bottom edge, ~25-30 dB below the knee (a boundary artifact of the power-choice rule): #10 q8, #232 q5/q6. C1-C6 classify the map, not a pathological chosen power; this class predicts the need for a floor-raise re-run.

NEW:sub-linewidth-shift — dressed-bare separation smaller than the dip linewidth, so no jump is visible even when the transition is inside the window; punch-out claims become unverifiable from the figure (q9 in every run, q7 in the evening runs).

NEW:resolution-mismatch — a frequency span so wide that a real few-MHz branch step spans about one pixel, making a true C1 map read as C3 bare-only (#9 q8). The taxonomy implicitly assumes the window resolves the structure.

Fit-semantics trap worth documenting: this node's 'frequency_shift' is the delta versus the previously stored resonator frequency (update delta), NOT the dressed-bare separation — q4's -25 kHz 'shift' coexists with a few-linewidth visible branch separation, and q9's shifts across four runs all reconstruct the same prior stored value.
golden_path_hints: Wasted/redundant runs: #8 (ceiling at 0 dBm bought only the bistable-chaos region for q9, and its q8 'success' at 5.9296 GHz / shift -22 MHz is a FALSE ACCEPT on a spur — exclude from any answer key); #9 (floor -70 + ~80 MHz span: both targets drowned, fully redundant); #232 half-wasted (floor -60 reproduced the bottom-edge-optimum pathology, redone a minute later). The morning could have been #7 -> #10 -> #11 (skip #8/#9); the evening could have been #233 alone. The working recipe on this setup: pmin=-45, pmax=-15..-20, per-resonator narrow spans; floors at or below about -55 dBm reliably push the reported optimum onto the scan edge/noise. Final correct values (last trustworthy success per qubit): q3 5.948468 GHz @ -41.8 dBm and q4 6.100153 GHz @ -39.5 dBm (run #12, morning bias state); q5 6.002704 GHz @ -37.1 dBm, q6 6.008323 GHz @ -36.5 dBm, q7 6.100350 GHz @ -36.5 dBm, q8 5.957756 GHz @ -35.2 dBm (run #233, evening state — q5-q8 moved ~3-6 MHz from morning, so #12's values for them are superseded); q9 6.168617 GHz @ -29.5 dBm (run #11, morning state only — never re-verified in the evening, so its evening-state value is unknown). #10's q8 optimum of -61.7 dBm and #232's q5/q6 optima (-57.9/-56.8 dBm) are scan-edge artifacts, not physical optima.

taxonomy_gaps: Unresolved-shift: when the dressed-bare separation is comparable to or smaller than the dip linewidth (small chi, e.g. q7 here), the map shows a single non-shifting dip even though the qubit is alive and punch-out is physically present. C2 blames the ceiling, C3 blames the floor or a dead qubit — neither names small dispersive shift as the cause.

C3 conflates two causes with opposite remedies: 'qubit far-detuned/dead' (nothing to gain from re-running) vs 'power floor too high' (fixable by deepening the floor — exactly what #347->#348 did). The taxonomy should split them, since the session evidence (adjacent runs) is often what disambiguates.

Fallback-fit pathology: the node can report success=true with a fitted frequency and a frequency_shift while simultaneously flagging 'no punch-out' and defaulting optimal power to the top of the window (#347). The map may be readable while the FIT is a degraded fallback; the taxonomy only classifies the map, not the fit's internal consistency.

Power-choice pathology: a correct two-branch map with a punch-out (C1) can still carry an optimal-power choice at the window floor where dip contrast is fading (#348 q7, #349 q6). C1-C6 describe the image, not whether the chosen power sits in the high-contrast part of the dressed branch.

Baseline structure: q6 carries a tall bright PEAK adjacent to the resonator dip at low power (impedance/interference structure, not a second resonator dip), which distorts the baseline the fitter sees. C5 covers multiple dips, not strong non-dip baseline features.

Bistable diagonal crossover: q6's transition is a diagonal walk of the dip between branches rather than a sharp snap — arguably C4, but C4's wording ('broad/noisy') doesn't capture the characteristic clean diagonal streak of a bistable transition region.

session_reading: A day of punch-out hunting across the chip's feedlines, with one lesson learned twice. Morning: q1 failed on a stale-seed frequency window (#40), was re-found with a wider span (#41), then the operator burned two identical repeats (#43, #44) instead of raising the power ceiling the node was explicitly asking for; the combined q1+q2 run with a high ceiling and high full-scale power (#135) finally produced textbook punch-outs for both. Evening: q6 succeeded twice (the second run with a much higher ceiling showing the full, rather gradual, crossover), then q12, q18 and q16 all failed the dressed-dip SNR gate — these are noise-floor failures, not window failures, but the operator kept reaching for window changes (wider frequency for q12, higher ceiling for q18), which helped visibility only for q18 and fixed nothing. q14 closed the day with a clean first-try success and a narrow confirmation re-run. Net: 4 qubits resolved (q1, q2, q6, q14), 3 unresolved for the same SNR-floor reason (q12, q16, q18).
taxonomy_gaps: NEW:snr-floor — the dressed branch is missing because the signal falls below the receiver noise floor at low drive amplitude (lower part of the map is pure speckle), not because the power window is wrong. C2 blames the ceiling and C3 blames the floor/detuning; neither names the real, actionable cause (more averaging or higher full-scale power). Seen in #89, #90, #179; contributing in #175/#176.

NEW:off-window — no feature in the map, but a monotonic brightening toward one frequency edge betrays a resonance just outside the frequency span (stale seed frequency). C6 cannot distinguish truly-empty from mis-centered, and the fix is entirely different. Seen in #40.

C4 conflates two mechanisms: a smooth gradual pull of the dip across a broad power band (#76) versus a bistable/messy double-ridge transition zone (#176). They read very differently and imply different optimal-power safety margins.

No vocabulary for the saturated high-power zone above the punch-out (bright band at the top of #135/#192) where the minimum trace is meaningless — annotators need it to avoid reading trace excursions there as features.

Fit-honesty patterns the case taxonomy cannot express: failed fits echoing stale pre-run seed values as if measured (#40); failed fits reporting an optimal power at or below the swept floor (#175: ~floor, #176: below floor); and punchout=true claimed from a window showing a single branch, with a bare value contradicting the same qubit's wide-window run (#213).

session_reading: A full-chip punch-out calibration day. Morning: q4 was tuned with three progressively re-framed windows (wide, then ceiling-clipped, then bracketing the transition) — the middle run truncated the punch-out and produced a bogus bare frequency, so only two of the three were needed. Late morning the operator worked qubits one at a time (q8, q3, q7) with a standard -50..+10 window and clean C1 results. At midday a single 8-qubit batch run at -60..0 failed 7 of 8 targets on dressed-dip SNR (the lowered ceiling/shared power budget put the dressed rows under the noise floor), and the entire afternoon became one-qubit-at-a-time recovery: q11 recovered in one run, q9 took three (including a SUCCESS with the dressed marker visibly off the dip, and a refusal whose gate message read "SNR 5.4 < 5"), and q10 took five identical retries against a marginal SNR gate despite figures that showed a textbook punch-out from the first attempt. taxonomy_gaps: NEW:snr-floor — dressed branch drowned in the noise floor at the low-power end while structure is clearly visible at mid/high power; C3 implies a physics cause (detuned/dead qubit) but this is a measurement-SNR/averaging failure and re-running with a higher ceiling or more averaging fixes it (most #335 targets).

Dispersive/multi-lobe lineshape: the response is an adjacent dip-plus-peak (Fano-like) rather than a simple dip, so 'dip position' is ill-defined for the tracker (q9/q13/q17/q18 in #335) — no C-case describes lineshape pathology.
Off-position fit on the correct line: a SUCCESS whose dressed marker sits a few linewidths off the visible dip (#342) — C5 covers wrong-LINE locks, nothing covers wrong-position on the right line.

Marginal-threshold refusal: node refuses a visually fittable map at the gate edge, including a message that reads as arithmetic nonsense after rounding ('SNR 5.4 < 5', #346) — a verdict/figure disagreement in the refusing direction.

Transition bistability: near the punch-out power the tracked dip hops between branches, so consecutive identical runs disagree on the bare frequency by several MHz (#348 vs #349; also the q4 and q7 bare spread across runs) — no case captures 'branches fine, bare unstable'.
Failure-path bookkeeping values: failed fits report an 'optimal power' below the swept floor — annotators need a flag saying these numbers are artifacts, not claims.

session_reading: A full-day punch-out survey of the 20-qubit CQT chip, worked feedline by feedline. After morning window-tuning on q4 and a few clean singles, a multiplexed all-qubit attempt (#335, pmin=-60 pmax=0) failed 7 of 8 targets, and the operator fell back to one qubit at a time, iterating windows per qubit: five attempts on q10 (four wasted identical retries before re-centering the frequency window fixed an edge-clipped resonator), two on q16 (raised pmax — the wrong knob for a low-power-SNR failure; q16 never passed), and two on q19 (raised pmin, which worked and set the trimmed window used for the rest of the sweep). From there q15, q18, q20, q1, q5 all passed in single attempts, and the day closed with a verification re-run of q8. The strategy converged, but the knob choices were reactive: the same SNR-floor failure got a different (and sometimes wrong) remedy each time.
taxonomy_gaps: SNR-floor failure: punch-out geometry present but the dressed branch drowns in the noise floor well above the power minimum — the bottom third of the map is pure speckle. Distinct from C4 (the physics is not smeared; the averaging/power floor is the limit). Seen on q10 #350/#351 and q16 #357/#359.

Edge-clipped line: the resonator sits at or beyond the edge of the frequency window (mis-centered window), often with a spurious feature mid-window getting mis-identified as bare. q10 #348-#351. None of C1-C6 name a window-placement failure.

Shallow-dip / weak-contrast: a feature exists but its depth is comparable to baseline ripple across the whole map, so branch structure is unresolvable — not C6 (not empty) and not C4 (no visible branches to smear). q19 #377/#378.
Bright companion streak: a narrow saturated-bright vertical streak immediately adjacent to the dressed dip at low power (q15 #368) — normalization or interference artifact with no taxonomy slot.

Marginal-optimal on a nominal success: the node reports success but places the optimal power at the extreme bottom row of the swept range (q19 #378, in noise) or at the immediate foot of the transition (q5 #394) — the taxonomy classifies the map, but has no way to flag a suspect power choice on an otherwise-passing run.
golden_path_hints: Wasted/redundant: q10 runs #348-#351 were four identical retries of a mis-centered window — the first map already showed the resonator clipped at the right edge, so the session could have jumped straight to the #352 fix (window re-centered ~+30 MHz). #481 (q8) duplicates the morning's passing #322 and only earns its place as a drift check. The multiplexed #335 window (-60..0 dBm) was the wrong shape — ceiling too low for punch-out and floor deep in noise — and cost a full per-qubit re-sweep. q16's retry #359 changed the wrong knob (pmax 10->15) for a dressed-dip-SNR failure; the remedy that worked on q19 (raise pmin -50->-40, #378) was never tried on q16, which ended the day uncalibrated (best unverified numbers: dressed ~5.8336 GHz, bare ~5.8309 GHz). Final correct values from the passing runs: q10 f_r=5.4234 GHz (bare 5.4171), optimal -19.1 dBm, FSP 16 dBm / amp 0.0177 V; q15 f_r=5.6991 GHz (bare 5.6826), -32.0 dBm, FSP -2 / amp 0.0317; q19 f_r=5.9092 GHz (bare 5.9056), optimal -39.1 dBm but this sits on the window's bottom row in noise — re-derive before trusting; q18 f_r=5.5454 GHz (bare 5.5367), -10.2 dBm, FSP 16 / amp 0.0489; q20 f_r=5.7632 GHz (bare 5.7596), -10.8 dBm, FSP 10 / amp 0.0914; q1 f_r=4.9822 GHz (bare 4.9729), -16.3 dBm, FSP 16 / amp 0.0242; q5 f_r=5.2616 GHz (bare 5.2478), -9.1 dBm (thin margin below the punch-out bend), FSP 14 / amp 0.0699; q8 f_r=4.9909 GHz, -33.0 dBm, FSP 10 / amp 0.0071 (no bare reported). Efficient path for this chip: standard window pmin=-40, pmax=+15, frequency window centered on the state's readout frequency, one run per qubit; escalate by re-centering frequency if the dip hugs a window edge, and by raising pmin (not pmax) when the failure message is dressed-dip SNR.

session_reading: An afternoon of punch-out attempts on two qubits, all three failing the node's dressed-dip SNR gate. The default -60..0 dBm window puts its lower half beneath the measurement noise floor on this line, which is the common thread: q9 (#624) actually acquired a perfectly usable punch-out map (dressed dip in a mid-power band, snap toward the bare line at the top) yet was declared failed because the analysis hunts for the dressed dip down in the noise; q12 (#727) showed only a single non-shifting line. The operator's one adaptation - shifting q12's window up 20 dB and widening the frequency span (#728) - was the right instinct for the noise floor but did not resolve a dressed branch, and the two q12 fits contradict each other in shift sign. The session ended with no accepted fit for either qubit despite q9's data being good enough to read by eye.
taxonomy_gaps: Noise-floor-limited window: the branch structure (even a full punch-out) is visible in the upper part of the power window while the lower part is pure measurement noise, so the dressed-frequency fit and the optimal-power search land in noise. C2 covers a ceiling below the punch-out; nothing covers a floor below the noise. Seen in all three runs; #624 is the clean example.

Fit-internally-inconsistent metadata: the recorded shift does not equal (dressed - bare) in the same fit record, and consecutive runs of the same qubit report opposite-sign shifts. This is a fit-quality pattern, not a data-geometry case, but annotators need a slot for it.

Analysis-vs-figure verdict mismatch: the node marks the run failed while the figure shows a textbook punch-out (the gate evaluates the dressed dip in the noisiest rows). A case label describing 'good data, wrong gate' would separate these from genuinely bad acquisitions.
golden_path_hints: q9 (#624): the figure supports bare ~5.2511 GHz (matches the node's bare estimate) and a dressed dip at ~5.252-5.2525 GHz, visible roughly between -35 and -10 dBm, with punch-out near -8 to -5 dBm. A sensible optimal readout power is ~-20 to -30 dBm (inside the visible dressed band); the node's reported dressed 5.2543 GHz and optimal -43 dBm are both wrong (the latter is in pure noise). The session could have ended for q9 after #624 by reading these values manually - no re-run was needed, only a re-read. q12: undetermined by this session. The only solid fact is a fixed line at ~5.8397-5.840 GHz (likely the bare or an un-punched resonance); neither #727's +7.8 MHz nor #728's -14 MHz claimed shift is trustworthy (mutually contradictory, neither visible as a dip). #728 was a reasonable, non-redundant retry, but the next step should have been more averaging/shots at low power (the SNR limit) rather than further window changes; a third window-only retry would have been wasted. Overall: zero runs in this batch produced an adopted calibration; the wasted effort is trusting any of the three fit outputs rather than any particular acquisition.

The crossover is a gradual S-bend rather than a sharp snap. session_reading: A day-long qubit-by-qubit punch-out survey of the CQT chip in which the operator's main lever was the power window, corrected reactively after each miss. The pattern repeats three times: a first attempt aimed too low (q15 #910 clipping the transition at its ceiling with half the window under the noise floor; q20 #995 failing the dressed-dip SNR gate; q6 #1116 entirely under the noise floor) followed within minutes by a raised window that produced a clean two-branch map (#914, #996, #1117) — the raise-the-window correction worked 3/3. The failures were q19, where the second attempt (#1089) moved the window DOWN instead of up and found nothing, leaving no trustworthy values for that qubit, and q12, whose resonator shows only a shallow asymmetric low-contrast feature in both runs (#1033, #1079), with the node nonetheless reporting success and placing its optimal power inside visibly noise-dominated rows. q7 (#1033) was a first-try textbook success.
taxonomy_gaps: Noise-floor-limited window: the lower portion of the power range is pure measurement noise so the dressed (low-power) branch is unmeasurable even though the resonator line itself is healthy — a window-vs-SNR failure distinct from C2/C3/C6 (seen in #910, #995, #1116, and the bottom rows of most maps). C3's 'power floor too high' is the opposite direction; there is no code for 'floor too LOW / window under the noise floor'.

Transition clipped at the window ceiling with partial onset visible: the per-row dip position starts deflecting in the top-most rows but the bare branch never establishes (#910, #995) — an in-between state that C2 ('only the dressed branch visible') does not quite express.

Low-contrast / asymmetric (Fano-like) line: a shallow local minimum riding a strongly sloped background with a bright peak-like ridge beside it, so the 'dip' identification itself is marginal (q12 in #1033 and #1079) — neither C4's smeared branches nor C5's multiple lines.

Chosen optimal power landing inside noise-dominated rows: a fit-output pathology orthogonal to the map's case classification (#985, #1079, borderline #1033-q12) — the map can be fine while the chosen operating point is not.

Gradual continuous S-bend crossover vs a discrete snap (#1117): C4 implies the fit is at risk, but a smooth bend with both plateaus visible is perfectly fittable — sharpness of the crossover and trustworthiness are not the same axis.
Per-row normalization artifacts at low power: saturated spike columns that dominate the color scale and can masquerade as a feature (#910).
golden_path_hints: Wasted/redundant runs: #910 (q15, window -50..0 clipped the punch-out and spent ~15 dB under the noise floor — superseded by #914 six minutes later), #995 (q20, floor too low — superseded by #996 one minute later), #1116 (q6, entire window under the noise floor — superseded by #1117 one minute later), #1089 (q19, window lowered to -50..0 after an already-marginal #985; the correction that worked everywhere else was raising the ceiling, so this run answered a question nobody should have asked), and #1079 (q12) is a near-duplicate of #1033 with the same window returning 5.84076 vs 5.84176 GHz — defensible as a post-recalibration consistency check but added little. Final correct values (the keepers): q15 -> #914: dressed 5.69639 GHz, bare 5.69389 GHz, optimal -9.4 dBm at FSP 11 dBm (amp 0.0959 V). q20 -> #996: dressed 5.76204 GHz, bare 5.75804 GHz, optimal -6.5 dBm at FSP 0 dBm (amp 0.4726 V). q6 -> #1117: dressed 5.42177 GHz, optimal -11.8 dBm at FSP 16 dBm (amp 0.0408 V). q7 -> #1033: dressed 5.55228 GHz, bare 5.55078 GHz, optimal -16.0 dBm at FSP 2 dBm (amp 0.1259 V). q12 -> #1079 nominally final (5.84076 GHz, optimal -29.0 dBm at FSP 2 dBm) but low-trust: contrast is marginal and the optimal sits in noise-dominated rows. q19: no trustworthy result in this batch — #985's 5.90964 GHz / -30.8 dBm is weakly supported and #1089 found nothing; the unexplored fix was a HIGHER window (ceiling above +10 dBm). Golden path: every successful map in this session put its transition between roughly +4 and -10 dBm, so a first-guess window of about [-30, +14] dBm would likely have made #910, #995, #1116, and #1089 unnecessary — the session's failures all came from windows biased 15-25 dB too low, and rows below about -35 dBm contributed nothing anywhere.

session_reading: Two distinct sessions in one day. In the early morning the operator hand-tuned q15 alone: a wide power survey (#1212) whose bottom third was noise and whose fit landed off the dip, immediately corrected by re-windowing (#1213, floor raised, ceiling extended), which produced the day's one textbook punch-out fit. Six hours later they switched to production mode: a fixed -40..0 window run over a 5-qubit subset (#1350), then two back-to-back full 11-qubit passes (#1351, #1352). The well-coupled resonators (q10, q11, q14, q18, q9, q15) fit reproducibly across the repeats, but the marginal-SNR set (q16, q17, q19, q20) flip-flopped between S and F on identical settings — the #1352 retry reshuffled the failures rather than resolving them, and q20 never passed. The fixed shared window has insufficient low-power SNR for that subset; repetition without changing averaging or per-qubit windows was not going to converge.
taxonomy_gaps: SNR-floor: the bottom N rows of the power window are pure noise and the dip is untraceable there — orthogonal to C1-C6 (co-occurs with C1 in #1212) and decisive when the analysis places the optimal power inside that region.

C3 conflates two causes: 'no dressed dip because the qubit is dead/far-detuned' vs 'no dressed dip because readout SNR at low power is insufficient'. All q20/q19 failures here are the SNR kind — the bare dip is sharp and healthy — and the remedy (more averaging / higher full-scale with lower amplitude) is entirely different from the dead-qubit case.

shift-unresolved: the dressed-bare separation is smaller than the linewidth/noise so the two branches are indistinguishable even though both may be inside the window (q16, q19, q12) — neither C2 (ceiling too low) nor C4 (branches visible but crossover broad) describes it.

bright-spike artifact: a narrow bright (peak, not dip) vertical streak adjacent to the resonance at low powers (q15 in every run, reaching an order of magnitude above baseline) — not a second resonator, but a fit-bias hazard the taxonomy cannot name.

bare-frequency-contradiction: the node's reported bare frequency lands in featureless background or on the opposite side of the dressed branch from where the figure shows the high-power branch moving (#1213 q15, q14 in both 11-qubit runs) — a fit-vs-figure defect class independent of the data geometry class.
verdict instability: S/F flickering across identical back-to-back runs on marginal-SNR features (q16 S/S/F, q17 S/F/S, q19 S/F/S) — a session-level pattern no per-run case can express.

shark-fin: a continuous smooth pull of the dip toward the bare side with a bright flank, rather than a discrete two-branch jump (q14) — sits between C1 and C4 and probably deserves its own name since the transition power is ill-defined.
golden_path_hints: q15: #1212 was a survey whose fit (5.6991 GHz, optimal -37.8 dBm) is unusable (frequency ~3 MHz high, power in the noise floor); #1213 is the keeper — dressed f_r = 5.6963 GHz, optimal -7.5 dBm at full-scale 13 dBm, with the true bare visibly ~5.6935-5.694 GHz (the fit's bare of 5.6825 GHz looks wrong). The three later q15 measurements (5.6963-5.6968) add nothing. #1350 (5-qubit subset) was superseded within a minute by the full passes — redundant except as a smoke test. #1351 vs #1352 are identical settings run twice; for the stable set one pass suffices: q10 5.4232 GHz / opt -19 dBm; q11 5.5586-5.5591 / opt -18..-20; q14 5.3217-5.3222 / opt -23 (bare claim 5.3077 dubious — figure pulls the other way); q18 5.5459-5.5464 / opt -10..-14; q9 5.2513-5.2518 / opt -12..-14 (beware the second resonance ~18 MHz above). The marginal set never produced trustworthy values: q12 ~5.839-5.840 (barely resolved), q16 ~5.832-5.833 (S/S/F flicker), q17 ~5.710 with optimal pinned at the window floor (-39/-40 — not credible), q19 5.9082/F/5.9102 (unusable), q20 never fit (bare ~5.759-5.762 clearly visible). The session could have ended after #1213 + ONE full-group pass IF that pass had used more averaging (or per-qubit power windows / higher full-scale with lower amplitude) for q16/q17/q19/q20 — the #1352 repeat at identical settings was predictably a coin-flip on exactly those four.
